Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor
assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6, all read for the
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the model's state space with
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$, and let $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ be its
componentwise Schwartz class
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]). Units are
those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the unit of angular
momentum is the unit of action (J$\,$s).

**(b) Orbital angular momentum.** For $i=1,2,3$ let $L_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint operator on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]], the Stone
generator of the coordinate rotation group $t\mapsto U(R_{i}(t))$, so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ and, on the Schwartz class,
$$L_{i}\psi=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}\,Q_{j}P_{k}\psi$$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clause (b),
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The model reads
$(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an **assigned sharp observable**, called the
$i$-th **orbital angular momentum** of the model, with outcome law
$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho}$ in a preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),(b),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). The operators
$L_{i}$ act on the spatial factor only; their reading on the angular degrees
of freedom is the one supplied by the sphere operators
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], and the finite-blocks identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ on the harmonic span is the content of a
separate lemma of this page
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]]).

**(c) Spin angular momentum.** Let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the internal
operators of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause
(c), the matrix actions $\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)_{l}=\hbar\sum_{m}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}$
of the self-adjoint matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]. The model reads
$(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the $i$-th **spin
angular momentum**; on the internal factor,
$$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k},\qquad S^{2}:=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c),
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)). The
**ladder** operators $S_{\pm}:=S_{x}\pm iS_{y}$ and the finite projections on
the basis vectors $e_{m}$ are structural objects of the internal factor, not
assigned sharp observables, and $S_{\pm}$ are not self-adjoint. For $s=\tfrac12$
one has $S_{i}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{i}$ in the Pauli matrices
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)). The internal
factor is a finite-dimensional bookkeeping factor: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Total angular momentum.** For each $i$ let
$$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}:=L_{i}+S_{i},\qquad D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}):=D(L_{i}),$$
the self-adjoint sum of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c)
(well defined because $S_{i}$ is bounded and strongly commutes with $L_{i}$;
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] clause (a),
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). The model reads
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the
$i$-th **total angular momentum**; its flow is the coordinate subgroup
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ of the lifted rotation action,
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clauses (b),(c)).

**(e) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the angular momentum vocabulary
of this page within P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited readings. No new
physical assumption is added; in particular no magnetic coupling, no
spin-orbit interaction, no SU(2) gauge structure and no anomaly is
introduced. Whether a laboratory angular momentum measurement is described by
one of the assigned pairs $(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$, $(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ or
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ is a tested identification with
uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a
consequence of this definition; no measurement procedure, apparatus,
resolution or empirical value is supplied here. Antiunitary symmetries,
superselection rules and symmetries of preparations as opposed to dynamics
are outside the definition.

Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$, together with the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]], and
assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]) and the readings of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Let $V:\mathbb
R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be real, bounded and measurable with
$V\circ R^{-1}=V$ almost everywhere for every $R\in SO(3)$, let
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
be the model's spin-independent bounded-potential energy operator on
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with flow
$U(t)=e^{-itH_{V}/\hbar}$ in the reading of P4, and let
$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}=L_{i}+S_{i}$ be the total angular momenta of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause
(d). Then:

(a) for each $i$ the lifted coordinate rotation family
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c) is a
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group of symmetries of the declared
dynamics: $U_{s}(A_{i}(t))\,U(u)=U(u)\,U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ for all $t,u$ and
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$;

(b) each $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is a conserved assigned sharp observable of
the model with energy $H_{V}$: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
and for a unit vector $\psi\in D(L_{i})=D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}})$ the mean and
the second moment of the law of $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ in the pure
preparation $[\psi(t)]$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero
values $\langle J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and
$\|J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\psi\|^{2}$;

(c) in the same situation each spin component $S_{i}$ and each orbital
generator $L_{i}$ is a conserved assigned sharp observable in the same sense,
the laws of $S_{i}$ and $L_{i}$ being time-independent in every preparation;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
cited results, and concerns the declared isolated model with a real bounded
measurable potential invariant under every spatial rotation. It asserts no
symmetry of any concrete external field or apparatus, excludes spin-dependent,
singular and unbounded potentials (which require their own domain and symmetry
arguments), introduces no measurement, detector or empirical record, and
makes no claim that a definite numerical value of $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is
revealed at each time: the conserved object is the outcome law.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the locally absolutely continuous causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, and let $B_R\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be the open ball of radius $R>0$ centered at $0$, with Euclidean norm $|\cdot|$. Suppose $(s,\sigma):U\to I\times B_R$ is a diffeomorphism of an open set $U\subseteq M$, satisfying:

**(C1)** $\partial_s$ is future timelike and every $s$-level is spacelike;

**(C2)** there is $K\ge1$ such that $|d\sigma(v)|\le Kds(v)$ for every nonzero future causal vector $v$ based in $U$.

Write $S=s^{-1}(0)$, and compute the domains of dependence intrinsically in $U$:
$$D^+_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D^-_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\}.$$
Here inextendibility means absence of an endpoint limit in the specified open submanifold, and Cauchy intersection means exactly one parameter visit ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). Then:

**(a)** $D^+_U(S)\subseteq\{s\ge0\}$ and $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$.

**(b)** The corrected open collar
$$Q=\{q\in U:|\sigma(q)|+K|s(q)|<R\}$$
is a neighborhood of the entire slice $S$ in $U$ and is contained in $D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)$; more precisely $Q\cap\{s>0\}\subseteq D^+_U(S)$ and $Q\cap\{s<0\}\subseteq D^-_U(S)$.

**(c)** The open set $W=\operatorname{int}_U(D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S))$ contains $Q$, and $S$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(W,g|_W,N|_W)$. Consequently $W$ is globally hyperbolic by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(d) Generic spacelike and noncompact scope.** For every smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subseteq M$ without boundary there exist an open neighborhood $U_\Sigma$ of $\Sigma$, a smooth positive function $\delta:\Sigma\to(0,\infty)$, and a diffeomorphism
$$F:\Omega\to U_\Sigma,\qquad\Omega=\{(s,x)\in\mathbb R\times\Sigma:|s|<\delta(x)\},\qquad F(0,x)=x,$$
such that $s$ is temporal and $F_*\partial_s$ is future timelike. The intrinsic set $W_\Sigma=\operatorname{int}_{U_\Sigma}(D^+_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma)\cup D^-_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma))$ is an open neighborhood in which $\Sigma$ is Cauchy, hence is globally hyperbolic. Neither compactness nor global acausality of $\Sigma$ in $M$ is assumed. No positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), carrying the analytic uniqueness and causal-curve supplier hypotheses.

Let a smooth reduced dust solution have a nondegenerate tentative orthonormal frame for $\gamma$ of signature $(+---)$, a metric-compatible tentative connection, reconstructed algebraic Weyl tensor $C$, prescribed curvature $\overline R$, and dust Schouten tensor $S$ as in [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] and [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. Allow $r\geq0$, with a smooth unit timelike $U$ prescribed also where $r=0$. Assume the parallel-comoving gauge and precisely the reduced equations
$$e_0=U,\quad\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0,\quad T^i{}_{0a}=0,\quad\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0,\quad P_{ab}=Q_{ab}=0,\quad q=U(r)+r\chi=0.$$
Here $a,b=1,2,3$, the first torsion index is the output index, and $P_{ab},Q_{ab}$ are the symmetric tracefree evolution projections of [[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]]. No spatial torsion or spatial curvature residual is assumed zero. Define $F_{jkl}=\nabla^i(C_{ijkl}-\gamma_{i[k}S_{l]j})$, $P_a=F_{0a0}$, and $Q_a=-\epsilon_a{}^{bc}F_{0bc}/2$. Then the spatial components of $(T,\Delta)$ and the vectors $(P,Q)$ satisfy the explicit closed linear homogeneous system constructed in the proof. Its principal part is transport along $U$ for $T,\Delta$ and the curl pair
$$e_0(P_a)+\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(Q_c),\qquad e_0(Q_a)-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(P_c).$$
It is symmetric hyperbolic on every spacelike initial hypersurface, including one tilted relative to $U$. If all residuals vanish initially, they vanish on its metric domain of determination. Consequently the tentative connection is Levi--Civita, its actual curvature equals $\overline R$, and the resulting metric satisfies the full Einstein-dust equation. The conclusion uses neither division by $r$ nor hypersurface orthogonality of $U$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]), carrying the analytic uniqueness and causal-curve supplier hypotheses.

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth spacelike initial surface with smooth induced Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_XN,Y)$, rest-mass density $\rho_{\rm mass}\ge0$, fixed $c>0$, and a prescribed smooth future $\gamma$-unit velocity $U_0$, where $\gamma=-g$ has signature $(+---)$. Put $\varepsilon=\rho_{\rm mass}c^2$. Assume the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the initial stress tensor $T_0=\varepsilon U_0^{\flat_g}\otimes U_0^{\flat_g}$, coupling $\kappa>0$ and cosmological constant $\Lambda$. The two lowered factors give the same covariant tensor with $\gamma=-g$. Choose an orientation and oriented tetrads locally for the magnetic contractions. Then locally:

(a) Gauss/Codazzi and the spatial target Ricci equations determine a unique full algebraic curvature tensor. Its full proper Lorentz basis transformation to an oriented tetrad with $e_0=U_0$, followed by the observer electric and magnetic contractions, determines $E_0,B_0$. Boosts may mix these parts.

(b) The tangential metric connection from $(h,K)$, differentiated boost data, and $\omega(U_0)=0$ uniquely determine the entire initial tetrad connection.

(c) At the first jets supplied by the reduced system, every initial torsion, curvature, matter-conservation and Bianchi residual vanishes. In particular the required direction-slot projections are $T^i{}_{0a}=0$ and $\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0$.

(d) For a future-positive timelike initial conormal $\zeta$, $z=\zeta(U_0)>|w|$ with $w_a=\zeta(e_a)$, the remaining Bianchi components obey $zP+\tfrac12w\times Q=0$, $zQ-\tfrac12w\times P=0$, so vanish. The initial time matrices are positive for every tilt $|v|<1$. Vacuum points remain admitted with prescribed auxiliary velocity.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let a perfect-fluid model have smooth equation of state $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an
open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let
$(\Sigma,h,K_2,\epsilon_0,n_0)$ be smooth initial data: a three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric $2$-tensor $K_2$, a smooth
function $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and a smooth future-directed unit timelike
vector field $n_0$ on $\Sigma$ (not required to be normal). Suppose the
constraint equations of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold on
$\Sigma$ with the stress-energy tensor computed from $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$. Then
the data admit a local development in the sense of
[[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$, a
smooth function $\epsilon$ and a smooth future-directed unit timelike field $n$
near $\Sigma$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\bigl((\epsilon+p)n_an_b+p\,g_{ab}\bigr),\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+h^{ba}\partial_ap=0$$
with $p=p(\epsilon)$ and $D,\vartheta,a,h$ as in
[[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]], with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data
$(h,K_2)$ and matter data $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$; and any two developments of the
same data agree near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix constants $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and a smooth mass-normalized density $\rho_0\ge0$. Specify initial velocity as a smooth section $U_0$ of $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with the bundle metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, satisfying $g_0(U_0,U_0)=-1$ and positive $N$ coefficient. Thus the velocity need not be normal and does not presuppose a spacetime development. Put $\varepsilon_0=\rho_0c^2$ and require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for $T_0=\varepsilon_0U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}$. On $\{\rho_0>0\}$ this is exactly the dust supplier with density parameter $\varepsilon_0$, rather than $\rho_0$ ([[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]); zero regions have independently prescribed velocity.

Then there is a smooth local development: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian metric $g$, density $\rho\ge0$ and future unit timelike field $u$ near an embedded copy of $\Sigma$, solving
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\rho c^2u_au_b,\qquad \nabla_uu=0,\qquad u(\rho)+\rho\nabla\!\cdot u=0.$$
The induced geometric and matter data are $(h,K,\rho_0,U_0)$, with $\mathcal V$ identified by $aN+X\mapsto an+i_*X$ using the future unit normal $n$. The initial surface lies in the interior of its domain of dependence; restriction to its Cauchy neighborhood gives a local Cauchy development. Every two such developments agree near $\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\rho,u$. No division by density is used, so smooth empty regions are admitted. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; no uniform noncompact slab or continuation past flow crossings is asserted.

Let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be the scalar-field matter model of
[[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with smooth potential $V$, and let
$(\Sigma,h,K_2,\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ be smooth initial data: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric $2$-tensor $K_2$, and smooth
functions $\varphi_0,\pi_0$ on $\Sigma$ (the scalar value and its prescribed
normal derivative). Suppose the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold on $\Sigma$, computed with
the scalar stress-energy tensor determined by $(h,K_2,\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ and the
chosen unit normal. Then the data admit a local development in the sense of
[[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ and
scalar field $\varphi$ near $\Sigma$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab},\qquad \Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$$
with $T$ the scalar stress tensor, $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced metric $h$ and
second fundamental form $K_2$, and $\varphi|_\Sigma=\varphi_0$,
$\partial_n\varphi|_\Sigma=\pi_0$; and any two such developments of the same
data agree near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and $c>0$ be constants, let $\Sigma$ be a smooth
three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$ and symmetric $2$-tensor $K$,
and suppose smooth matter initial data and a matter sector are given in one of
the following four branches, with the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] satisfied:

1. **vacuum with cosmological constant:** no matter fields; the constraints
   read $S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|^2_h=2\Lambda$ and
   $\operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=0$;
2. **scalar field:** a model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ as in
   [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with smooth potential and initial data
   $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$;
3. **strict barotropic perfect fluid:** a model with smooth $p=p(\epsilon)$ and
   $\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$, with initial data
   $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]);
4. **geodesic dust:** an energy-coefficient density $\varepsilon_0\ge0$
   with prescribed smooth future unit velocity $U_0$, as a section of
   $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$ with metric $-ab+h(X,Y)$.
   On positive-density regions this is the model $(\varepsilon,u)$ of
   [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; through zero-density regions its smooth
   unit velocity is separately prescribed and required to remain geodesic.
   Its source is $T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$.

Then in each branch there is a smooth local development with the properties
established in the corresponding item, [[thm-gr-scalar-field-local-evolution]]
(branch 2), [[thm-gr-barotropic-fluid-local-evolution]] (branch 3),
[[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]] (branch 4) and, for branch 1, the vacuum
instance of [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric
$g$ with $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced data $(h,K)$, solving
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ with the branch's stress tensor and matter
equations, with $\Sigma$ in the interior of its domain of dependence, and with
uniqueness near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

Statement

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]).

Adopt the direct-equation presentation of the classical gravitational framework
for a model satisfying the spacetime and classical-domain postulate
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the field-and-matter postulate
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], with the field law
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]]: on the matter domain of the model,
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab},\qquad \kappa=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4},$$
with $T$ the stress-energy tensor of the model's selected matter sector. Let the
sector be one of:

1. vacuum with cosmological constant ($T=0$);
2. the scalar-field model $(\varphi,V,K)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]
   with a chosen smooth potential whose scalar equation and stress tensor are
   those defined there;
3. the perfect-fluid model of [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]] with a
   smooth barotropic equation of state satisfying $\epsilon+p>0$ and
   $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ on the range of the data;
4. an energy-coefficient dust density $\varepsilon\ge0$ and prescribed
   smooth future unit velocity, with $T=\varepsilon u^\flat\otimes u^\flat$.
   On positive-density regions this is [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]];
   on zero-density regions the velocity is separately prescribed and the
   geodesic equation remains imposed. Equivalently the mass-normalized
   density is $\rho=\varepsilon/c^2$.

Let $(\Sigma,h,K)$ with the sector's smooth initial data (respectively nothing,
$(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$, $(\epsilon_0,n_0)$, $(\varepsilon_0,U_0)$) satisfy the constraint
equations [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the sector's
stress tensor. Then the model admits a **local Cauchy development**: there are
a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of the framework and
a spacelike embedded image of $\Sigma$ inducing $(h,K)$ and the stated matter
data, solving the field law $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ and the
sector's matter equations on a neighborhood of $\Sigma$; $\Sigma$ lies in the
interior of its domain of dependence; and any two such developments of the same
data agree near $\Sigma$ up to an isometry fixing the data and the time
orientation. The development is local in time and no uniform-in-the-data
existence time or global statement is asserted.

This page contains the Gr14 high-regularity symmetric hyperbolic proof material:
the periodic first-order theory (E0), the harmonic-gauge reduced Einstein
equation and its subsidiary system (E1), the geometric data and local
development theorems (E2), and the selected matter reductions with the complete
geodesic-dust residual chain (E3, E3d--E3d.2). Its content assumes Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for local analytic extraction and manifold patching, and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]) for the causal-curve calculus in the Cauchy-neighborhood argument. Its physical content is conditional:
the physical reading is the model deduction of
[[pthm-gr-high-regularity-local-development]] from the adopted postulates
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] and the matter definitions
[[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; the mathematical carriers are
[[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] and its prerequisites.
